artworks.title: Drunken Silenus
artworks.description: Ribera's Capodimonte canvas: the aged companion of Dionysus sprawls naked and laughing while satyrs crown him with vine — Silenus as flesh, wine, and prophecy.

artworks.title: Drunken Silenus
artworks.description: Van Dyck's Pushkin painting: Silenus supported by satyrs in a swirl of wine-skin and flesh — the tutor of Bacchus too drunk to stand alone.

artworks.title: Bacchanalia
artworks.description: Rubens fills the Pushkin canvas with Silenus at the center of the revel — heavy, crowned, and half-asleep amid nymphs and goats.

artworks.title: The sleeping Silenus (Byzantine silver relief)
artworks.description: Silver relief stamped in the reign of Justinian I (Washington, Dumbarton Oaks): the drunken Silenus asleep, about to be woken by a satyr blowing a trumpet in his ear.
